Header: Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV) Chichewa: Chisaka cha nthochi

Prevention: Virus (BBTV) which is transmitted by aphids.
The disease attacks all stages of the banana crop.
Do not take planting materials from plants which display symptoms.
Avoid movement of planting materials from infected fields to non-infected fields.
Promote natural enemies of the virus-transmitting aphids, like (Parasitoids:
Lysiphlebus testaceipes, .fabarum, Ephedrus cerasicola ; Predators: ladybird beetles and spiders).
Introduce practices that will attract natural enemies for control of aphids, e.g. permaculture and intercropping.
Where applicable, observe isolation distance (buffer zone) of 100m between old and new banana plantations.
Monitoring: Monitor all year round at two week intervals.
Infected leaves are erect, narrow, bunchy, stunted, and often have yellow leaf margins.
Presence of dark-green long thin spots on the petioles, midribs, and leaf veins of the newly emerging leaves.
New fully opened leaves are smaller in size than older ones which is the opposite of the normal banana plant.
Dark green hooked lines on leaves next to midribs.
Infected plants rarely produce a fruit, but if they do, the fruit stalk is small and distorted.
If 1 banana plant shows symptoms in your field, consider action.
If neighbouring fields are infected, consider vector control.
Direct Control: Spray pressurised water at aphids to remove them from plants and reduce disease transmission.
Uproot affected banana plants immediately, cut into small pieces, dry in the sun or bury to prevent aphids spreading disease to other plants.
Chop and sprinkle a lot of salt on the fresh banana corm pieces, then bury them to control the disease.
Azadirachtin (Nimbecidine) 50-60ml/20L of water or 2.5L/ha. 3-4 applications can be used at intervals of 15-20 days to control the aphid vector.
Apply soapy water to wash off aphids.
Restrictions: Keep pesticides out of reach of children.
Dispose of containers responsibly (do not clean containers near water).

Usually applied at 125g of chemical with 100L of water, but check product label.
Intervals of 2 weeks between sprays, max 2 sprays per season; WHO toxicity class
II (moderately acute hazardous to humans); This insecticide stiffens leaves of the plants; p.h.i. 14 days, r.e.i. half day.
There is no pesticide against the virus disease.
An infected plant cannot be cured.
Only aphids may be controlled to prevent further disease spread, but chances are low to kill all aphids.
Spray in the morning and afternoon to avoid chemical evaporation.
Spray when not windy and no rains.
